A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WILDA research. All 29 pages of v2 and 32 pages of v3, including figures, tables, equations, appendices and checklists, support comparison. Relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original GLUE and MMLU experiments, cross-domain evaluations, stability measurements, adapter-fusion results and weak-to-strong generalization analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds ARC-Challenge results and an analysis of task-specific adapters during cross-task evaluation.

M1.justification: The teacher–student procedure, distribution-matching loss, LoRA adapters and fixed/shuffle/resample variants are unchanged. Adapter arithmetic already appears in v2 Section 3.3, and mixed adapter-plus-prompt inference already appears in v2 Appendix D.2.

E1.justification: v3 adds ARC-Challenge evaluation and cross-task scenarios such as SST-to-CoLA, MNLI-to-QQP and MRPC-to-SST in Table 11. Existing GLUE, MMLU and near-OOD coverage is retained.

E2.justification: The new cross-domain preservation comparison includes a zero-shot reference alongside 16-shot ICL and WILDA-S (Table 11); the earlier cross-domain comparison lacked that reference. Comparator memberships in matched existing experiments remain unchanged, and ARC-Challenge uses the established baseline family.

E3.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a testing design that leaves task-specific adapters enabled during evaluation on other tasks, with zero-shot performance as a control. Existing experimental settings are retained. ARC's evaluation split and sample size are unspecified, and Table 11's accuracy label is not reconciled with Section 3.1's CoLA and QQP metrics.

E4.justification: v3 adds a targeted analysis of whether an active task-specific adapter harms general performance (Appendix D.2, Table 11). Existing ordering-stability, weak-to-strong, reconstruction and few-shot analyses are retained; moving the few-shot analysis into Section 3.4 does not make it new.

E5.justification: Both versions specify 10-seed experiments, standard deviations, 50 ordering runs, and Wilcoxon and Levene tests with Holm-Bonferroni correction. Table 11 follows the existing repeated-run practice. No increased run count or new uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing result values, including Figure 2 and the relocated few-shot table, are unchanged. v3 adds ARC-Challenge scores, including 59.2 for WILDA-S versus 54.5 for standard ICL, and Table 11's cross-domain results. Its QNLI-to-RTE entry is not reconciled with retained Table 3, preventing a same-setting interpretation of their difference.

T1.justification: Section 2's equations and the derivations and mathematical relationships in Appendices A and B are retained. Appendix A renames subsections and merges its final interpretation into the preceding subsection without changing the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract and central claims about disentanglement, generalization, stability and efficiency are retained. v3 explicitly lists adapter arithmetic as a third contribution, but its composition and scalability claims already appear in v2 Sections 3.3 and 6.

C2.justification: v3 newly interprets the cross-task results as showing that an enabled task-specific adapter preserves general zero-shot capabilities. Section 4 also adds an explicit representation-smoothing interpretation. Appendix C's computational, unlabeled-data and large-demonstration limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository address, whereas v2 only states that code was supplied as supplemental material. The model table corrects Meta-Llama-3-8Bb to Meta-Llama-3-8B. Hardware, optimizer, LoRA settings and existing prompt templates are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Clark et al.'s ARC reference. The related-work discussion is otherwise retained. Expanded author lists and publication-metadata updates refer to existing cited works rather than additional research.

P1.justification: v3 locally revises the introduction and conclusion, expands the explanation of the existing few-shot experiment and moves it from Appendix D.2 to Section 3.4. Appendix headings and supplementary-result summaries are refined, while most methodological and analytical prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 7 and 11, relocates v2 Table 9 to main-text Table 5, and reorganizes Table 1 into model blocks. Captions, table grouping and appendix pagination receive limited adjustments. Both figures retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: ARC-Challenge provides an additional test of the method on reasoning questions, while the explicit code pointer and clearer presentation of the existing few-shot experiment improve accessibility and assessability. These are limited gains over an otherwise stable paper. Their value is tempered by incomplete reporting of the added evaluations, especially the unexplained QNLI-to-RTE discrepancy between Tables 3 and 11.
